title: Tethering Broken Themes: Aligning Neural Topic Models with Labels and Authors
subcategory: supervised / aligned VAE topic model with label and author metadata
task: Aligning neural topics with document labels and authorship
problem: NTM topics often do not match human intent (labels may be merged or split), and author information is not used in NTMs.
architecture: FANToM, a plug-in for VAE-based NTMs: an expert-aligned Dirichlet prior built from a topic-label vector restricts each document's topics to its labels (expert alignment loss between posterior and prior; labels from experts or an LLM); a separate author decoder learns a multinomial over authors from the topic vector; both can be combined.
llm_or_encoder: Optional LLM as label assigner when expert labels are missing

datasets.name: arxiv
datasets.details: arXiv abstracts with author names (only dataset with authors)

metrics: Topic Quality TQ = C_V (WikiText-103 reference) x TD
key_results: FANToM on ECRTM, 20NG: Purity 0.710 and NMI 0.681 vs 0.628 and 0.617 for ECRTM alone.
FANToM on ECRTM, AGN: Purity 0.918 and NMI 0.873 vs 0.826 and 0.809.
strengths: Works on top of any VAE-based topic model.
Learns author-topic distributions in NTMs, enabling author interest and similarity analysis.

limitations.text: Needs labels and author metadata; LLM-based labelling adds compute cost and suffers from context-length truncation and limited multilingual small LLMs.
May fail when an author suddenly writes on an unrelated topic.
